card.title: Boltzmann Constant, Root Mean Square Speed and Heat Capacities

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **Boltzmann constant** $k_B = R/N_A = 1.38\times10^{-23}$ J/K is the gas constant per molecule — the exchange rate between temperature and molecular energy. Molecular speeds come in three averages from the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution: **most probable** $\sqrt{2k_BT/m}$, **average** $\sqrt{8k_BT/\pi m}$, and **rms** $\sqrt{3k_BT/m} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$ — in ratio 1.414 : 1.596 : 1.732.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Boltzmann Constant as Bridge:** $k_B = R/N_A = 1.38 imes 10^{-23}$ J/K connects microscopic ($k_B$) and macroscopic ($R$) thermodynamics. It relates energy per degree of freedom ($ rac{1}{2}k_B T$) to temperature.  ·  **Speed Hierarchy:** For the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution: $v_p = \sqrt{2RT/M}$, $ ar{v} = \sqrt{8RT/\pi M}$, $v_{rms} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$. The order is always $v_p <  ar{v} < v_{rms}$ with ratios $\sqrt{2} : \sqrt{8/\pi} : \sqrt{3} \approx 1.414 : 1.596 : 1.732$.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The rms speed of gas molecules is proportional to the square root of the absolute temperature."

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **M in kg/mol:** 32 g/mol must enter as 0.032 — the classic unit slip.  ·  **Three speeds, one order:** v_p < v̄ < v_rms (√2 : √8/π : √3).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Speed of a Molecule Molecules in a gas do not share one speed: they swarm across a distribution. Three averages describe it — rms, average and most-probable — and the Boltzmann constant k_B is the per-molecule currency in which temperature and energy are exchanged. NEB asks for the rms speed of oxygen at 27 °C almost every other year.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2022, 2024) ### 2.1 The Boltzmann constant $$k_B = \frac{R}{N_A} = \frac{8.31}{6.022\times10^{23}} = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \text{ J/K}$$ — the gas constant **per molecule**: R is for a mole, k_B for one molecule. It converts temperature to energy: $k_BT$ is the energy scale of molecular physics.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "√(3RT/M) with M in kg/mol; T in kelvin."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): Find the rms speed of nitrogen (M = 28 g/mol) at 27 °C.** — √(3×8.31×300/0.028) = 517 m/s.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: The identical 3m numerical appeared in 2022 and 2024 — a near-certain repeat.

rows.label: Classified table
rows.text: From $\frac{1}{2}m\bar{c^2} = \frac{3}{2}k_BT$: · Speed | Formula | Value (O₂ at 300 K) · **rms speed** | $v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3k_BT}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$ | 483 m/s · **Average speed** | $\bar{v} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8k_BT}{\pi m}}$ | 445 m/s · **Most probable speed** | $v_p = \sqrt{\dfrac{2k_BT}{m}}$ | 395 m/s

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The rms speed is the speed of a molecule carrying the average kinetic energy.**

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: k_B = R/N_A = 1.38×10⁻²³ J/K.  ·  v_rms = √(3RT/M) — 483 m/s for O₂ at 27 °C.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Hydrogen's rms speed (1.9 km/s at 300 K) approaches Earth's escape velocity (11.2 km/s) high in the thermosphere — planetary hydrogen loss.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The Boltzmann constant equals: → B  ·  NEB 2024: v_rms of O₂ at 27 °C ≈ → B

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Heat Capacity and DOF:** $C_V = rac{f}{2}R$, $C_P = C_V + R = rac{f+2}{2}R$, where $f$ is active degrees of freedom. Monatomic: $f=3$ (translational only). Diatomic: $f=5$ (3 trans + 2 rot) at room temp. Vibrational modes activate at high temperatures.  ·  Verified PYQs: rms speed of O₂ at 27 °C (2022, 2024 — 3m each).  ·  Why do light gases escape planets but heavy ones do not?
